Package gooeygui

package gooeygui
GooeyGUI: simple, object-oriented windows, buttons, and other graphical components for Java, built on top of Swing.

Add import gooeygui.*; to the top of your file, create a Window, then create components and add them to it. Every component's position is the (x, y) of its top-left corner, in pixels, measured from the top-left of the window. Y increases downward.

Running your code when something happens

Methods such as setOnClick and setOnChange take the name of a method to run, written as this::methodName. The method must be void and take no parameters. Because it uses this, set up your components in a constructor (or another non-static method), not in main.


 import gooeygui.*;

 public class CounterApp {
     private int count;
     private Label countLabel;

     public CounterApp() {
         Window window = new Window("Counter", 300, 200);
         countLabel = new Label("Count: 0", 100, 40, 100, 30);
         Button addButton = new Button("Add 1", 100, 90, 100, 30, this::addOne);
         window.addComponent(countLabel);
         window.addComponent(addButton);
     }

     public void addOne() {
         count++;
         countLabel.setText("Count: " + count);
     }

     public static void main(String[] args) {
         new CounterApp();
     }
 }

Errors

When a component is used incorrectly, GooeyGUI throws a GooeyGUIException that explains the problem and how to fix it, and points to the line in your code that caused it. If your own method crashes while running as a click or change action, GooeyGUI prints a short message pointing to your code and the program keeps running.

    The parent class of every visual GooeyGUI component, such as Button, Label, and TextField.
    Dropdown
    A drop-down menu that lets the user choose one text option from a list.
    FileChooser
    A pop-up dialog that lets the user browse for a file to open or a location to save a file.
    GooeyGUIException
    The error GooeyGUI throws when a component is used incorrectly, such as giving a button a negative width or selecting an index that does not exist.
    Image
    A picture loaded from an image file (.png, .jpg, or .gif) and stretched to fit the component's width and height.
    Label

    Panel
    A rectangular container that holds other components.

    A round option button with a text label.
    RadioGroup
    Links RadioButton objects together so that only one of them can be selected at a time.
